Bronze HMO.description: Lowest monthly cost, highest cost when you use care. HMO network: pick a primary care provider; referrals needed to see a specialist.

Silver PPO.description: Moderate monthly cost and moderate cost when you use care. PPO network: no referrals needed, and out-of-network care is covered at a lower rate.

Gold HMO.description: Highest monthly cost, lowest cost when you use care. HMO network: pick a primary care provider; referrals needed to see a specialist.

Basic Dental.description: Lower monthly cost. Preventive care (cleanings, exams) covered in full; a smaller share of major work like crowns or root canals.

Plus Dental.description: Higher monthly cost. Preventive care covered in full, a larger share of major work, and includes orthodontia coverage.

Standard Vision.description: One eye exam per year, plus an allowance toward glasses or contact lenses.

policy_library._note: Synthetic employer rules written for this demo. The FMLA entry summarizes federal basics for illustration only; it is not legal advice.

entries.title: Enrollment window
entries.text: New hires have 30 days from their start date to choose or waive each benefit. Missing the window requires an HR exception.

entries.title: Dependent proof
entries.text: Covering a spouse needs a marriage certificate; covering a child needs a birth certificate. A received document waits for HR verification, and the item stays open until HR verifies it. A tier that covers dependents cannot be approved without verified proof for each dependent.

entries.title: Benefits eligibility
entries.text: Medical, dental and vision require at least 30 scheduled hours per week. HR may approve a documented exception with a reason.

entries.title: Coverage start
entries.text: Coverage starts on the first day of the month after the start date.

entries.title: 401(k) match
entries.text: The employer matches 100% of the employee's contribution up to 4% of pay. The contribution amount is the employee's choice.

entries.title: Approved record is the source of truth
entries.text: If a carrier confirmation differs from the HR-approved record, the approved record stands until HR approves a change. HR asks the carrier to correct its record; nobody changes the approval to match the carrier.

entries.title: Leave documents
entries.text: Own health and family care leave need a medical certification; bonding leave needs a birth or placement record; personal leave needs no document. HR may request missing documents after submission.

entries.source: Demo summary of federal FMLA basics (29 CFR 825.110), illustration only
entries.title: FMLA pre-check basics
entries.text: FMLA basics are 12 months of service and 1,250 hours worked in the last 12 months. Not meeting them does not deny every option: HR also checks state leave and company policy. Unknown facts stay unknown.

entries.title: Clarification is not a decision
entries.text: Questions from an assistant help an employee prepare a request. They are not HR notices, approvals or denials.

entries.title: Who counts as a dependent
entries.text: Eligible dependents are a spouse and children. Parents, domestic partners not registered with HR, and other relatives are not eligible dependents under medical, dental or vision coverage, regardless of tier.

entries.title: 401(k) match vesting
entries.text: Your own contributions are always 100% yours. The employer match vests 25% per year of service and is fully yours after 4 years of service. Vesting only affects what happens to the match if you leave the company before it is fully vested; it does not affect your contribution choice today.
